To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conformation of peptides containing N-methylated amino acids can be predicted using quantum mechanics and molecular dynamics simulation methods.

N-methylation of alanine residues in peptides increases the proteolytical stability of peptides, and that the poly N-methylated peptides populate in helical structure in gas phase and beta-strand conformation in aqueous solution.

the poly N-MeAlanine peptide adopts helical structure without H-bond and the tetrapeptide containing alternating N-MeAlaNMeAla adopts beta-strand structure and interacts with Abeta15- 42 hydrophobic stretch.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conformational behavior and the interaction of peptides containing N-methylated residues.
the conformational behavior, stability and design of peptides containing N-methylated amino acids.
the conformational analysis of peptides with NMeAla and Ala residues at alternate positions and their use in designing peptide inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

N-MeAlanine containing peptides are stable in aqueous environment due to the presence of carbonyl-carbon interaction, and the helical structure is stabilized by carbonyls-carbonyls interactions, whereas beta-sheet structure is stabilized by solvent-solvent interactions.
N-methylation of peptide backbone increases the proteolytical stability and leads to increased helical and beta-strand structures.
NMeAla residue is an ideal residue for designing helical and beta-strand structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N-methylation of amino acid residues in the peptides increases their stability and the peptides containing only NMeAla residues are shown to populate in helical structure in water.
N-methylation increases the stability of peptides and the conformational behavior is governed by the solvent environment.
N-methylation of alanine residues increases the stability of peptides by preventing the formation of hydrogen bonds and leads to improved helical structure in aqueous solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
N-methylation can induce helical and beta-strand structure in peptides and can be used for the development of peptide-based drugs.
the poly-NMeAla peptides can be used as a template to design peptide inhibitors of protein-protein and protein-ligand interaction.
the NMeAla residues can stabilize the helical structure of peptides without hydrogen bond.
